title: h3spec HTTP/3 Server Conformance Pipeline Verification
verification_method: Build, requirement-home tests, plan-only h3spec runner execution, repo-local h3spec acquisition, parser smoke test, and SpecTrace validation.
scope: Verify that the repository exposes an advisory h3spec HTTP/3 server conformance pipeline that captures raw output, normalizes results, maps RFC 9114/RFC 9204 failures, and keeps failures as TODO/triage evidence until protocol-owned requirements close them.
procedure: Run `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/interop/http3-h3spec/Install-H3SpecTool.ps1 -PassThruJson` on platforms where Docker or a native release asset is available.
expected_result: The build and requirement-home tests pass, the acquisition path stores h3spec under `.artifacts/tools` without global PATH setup, the plan-only runner emits raw-log placeholders and parsed report artifacts, the parser maps sample HTTP/3 and QPACK failures to RFC 9114 and RFC 9204 TODO rows, and SpecTrace validation accepts the new artifacts.
evidence: 2026-05-25: `dotnet build Incursa.Quic.slnx -c Release --no-restore` passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.

status_summary: Passed for the advisory h3spec harness, repo-local acquisition path, parser, report, and CI-dispatch surfaces. The preserved plan-only evidence proves artifact generation only. The 2026-06-19 live local acquired-h3spec baseline run is advisory conformance triage: it executed 49 cases, reported 41 failures, and mapped 15 failures to RFC 9114/RFC 9204 follow-up areas. The 2026-06-19 HTTP/3-matched subset runs reported 6 failures out of 15 mapped cases after the production server-close behavior slice, 2 failures out of 15 mapped cases after the peer QPACK decoder-stream parsing slice, 3 failures out of 15 mapped cases after the request-stream CANCEL_PUSH frame-type validation slice where the targeted CANCEL_PUSH case passed, and 4 failures out of 15 mapped cases after the peer critical-stream EOF hardening slice where QPACK 4.2 remained a transport-boundary failure. These runs do not promote or demote production support claims until protocol-owned requirements and tests close the underlying behavior.
